techniques.name: HOLOGRAPH: Active Causal Discovery via Sheaf-Theoretic Alignment of LLM Priors
techniques.capability_enabled: LLM-guided active causal discovery that represents local causal beliefs as sheaf sections, handles hidden confounders via Algebraic Latent Projection, and uses Expected Free Energy to select maximally informative LLM queries (synthetic ER/SF and real Sachs benchmarks, 20-100 variables).
techniques.code_evidence: Search result states: 'Code and supplementary materials are available at: https://github.com/hyunjun1121/holograph' (repo also returned directly in GitHub search results).
techniques.verbatim_quote: HOLOGRAPH is a framework that formalizes LLM-guided causal discovery through sheaf theory--representing local causal beliefs as sections of a presheaf over variable subsets.

techniques.name: Large Causal Models (LCMs) for Temporal Causal Discovery
techniques.subfield: A: temporal causal discovery (pre-trained foundation model)
techniques.capability_enabled: Pre-trained neural architectures (foundation-model style) for temporal causal discovery, trained at scale by combining diverse synthetic generators with realistic time-series datasets; released model weights enable amortized inference of temporal causal structure.
techniques.code_evidence: Search result states: 'The experiments and model weights are available at github.com/kougioulis/LCM-paper/.' HuggingFace papers page also listed.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes Large Causal Models (LCMs), a class of pre-trained neural architectures specifically designed for temporal causal discovery, combining diverse synthetic generators with realistic time-series datasets.

techniques.name: CausalCompass: Robustness Benchmark for Time-Series Causal Discovery in Misspecified Scenarios
techniques.capability_enabled: Extensible benchmark suite to assess robustness of time-series causal discovery (TSCD) methods across eight assumption-violation scenarios; finds deep-learning approaches strongest overall and exposes preprocessing dependence (e.g., NTS-NOTEARS needs standardization).
techniques.code_evidence: Search result states: 'The code and datasets are available at https://github.com/huiyang-yi/CausalCompass'.
techniques.verbatim_quote: CausalCompass is a flexible and extensible benchmark suite designed to assess the robustness of time-series causal discovery (TSCD) methods under violations of modeling assumptions.

techniques.name: Beyond identifiability: Learning causal representations with few environments and finite samples
techniques.capability_enabled: Explicit finite-sample guarantees for causal representation learning from a sublinear (logarithmic) number of unknown multi-node interventions, with consistent recovery of the latent causal graph, mixing matrix/representations, and unknown intervention targets without pre-designed targets.
techniques.code_evidence: No code or weights link seen in search results; result explicitly notes 'the search results don't show a direct code link.' Primarily a theory/finite-sample paper.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The paper shows that causal representations can be learned with only a logarithmic number of unknown, multi-node interventions, and that intervention targets need not be carefully designed in advance.

techniques.name: Amortized Factor Inference Networks (AFINs) for Posterior Inference
techniques.capability_enabled: Encode-merge-decode inference networks built on dimension-independent modules that map a model specification plus observations to variational posterior parameters; a single trained AFIN matches NUTS-level posterior accuracy while needing 2-4 orders of magnitude less test-time compute.
techniques.code_evidence: Search result states: 'Code is available at https://github.com/joohwanko/AFINs' (authors Joohwan Ko and Justin Domke).
techniques.verbatim_quote: Amortized Factor Inference Networks (AFINs) are a family of encode-merge-decode inference networks built on dimension-independent modules that map a model specification and its observations to the parameters of a variational posterior.

techniques.name: Robust Simulation Based Inference Through Robust Optimal Transport
techniques.capability_enabled: Robust SBI under model misspecification using a Kullback-Leibler-informed robust Optimal Transport divergence; provides a stochastic sub-gradient ascent algorithm with convergence guarantees and a parallelized bootstrap-based SBI algorithm for parameter uncertainty quantification.
techniques.code_evidence: No paper-specific code repo seen; search returned only an unrelated robustOT repo (yogeshbalaji/robustOT, NeurIPS 2020) which is a different referenced work.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The authors introduce a stochastic sub-gradient ascent algorithm with a convergence guarantee for estimating the semi-discrete version of this robust Optimal Transport divergence, and design a parallelized SBI algorithm which employs the regular bootstrap on top of minimum semi-discrete robust Optimal Transport for parameter uncertainty quantification.

techniques.name: Bayesian Scattering: A Principled Baseline for Uncertainty on Image Data
techniques.subfield: B: Bayesian deep learning / uncertainty quantification
techniques.capability_enabled: A non-learned deep feature extractor (wavelet scattering transform) coupled with a simple probabilistic head, serving as a principled UQ baseline for images; validated under distribution shift (medical imaging institution shift, country-to-country wealth mapping) and for Bayesian optimization of molecular properties.
techniques.code_evidence: No GitHub repo for this paper found in search results; unrelated Bayesian-UQ repos were returned but none tied to 2603.20908.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The paper 'Bayesian Scattering: A Principled Baseline for Uncertainty on Image Data' (arXiv:2603.20908) proposes a method that couples the wavelet scattering transform—a deep, non-learned feature extractor—with a simple probabilistic head.

techniques.name: Amortized Simulation-Based Inference in Generalized Bayes via Neural Posterior Estimation
techniques.capability_enabled: First fully amortized variational approximation to the tempered (generalized-Bayes) posterior family by training a neural posterior estimator, enabling sampling in a single forward pass without simulator calls or inference-time MCMC.
techniques.code_evidence: No code repository link found in search results; result explicitly notes it 'don't show a direct link to the code repository.'
techniques.verbatim_quote: The paper 'Amortized Simulation-Based Inference in Generalized Bayes via Neural Posterior Estimation' (2601.22367) introduces the first fully amortized variational approximation to the tempered posterior family by training a neural posterior estimator that enables sampling in a single forward pass, without simulator calls or inference-time MCMC.
